profile.address: 2750, East Discovery Parkway, Bloomington, Monroe County, Indiana, 47408
profile.reading:
Located at 2750 East Discovery Parkway on the eastern edge of Indiana University's Bloomington campus, this building is IU's primary data center, run by University Information Technology Services (UITS) through its Data Center Operations group. It is one of two data centers UITS operates for the university system -- the other sits in Indianapolis, inside the Informatics and Communications Technology Complex -- and the Bloomington site is the larger and older of the two, having been in continuous operation for roughly a decade and a half by the mid-2020s (it was already described as "about a decade" old in a 2019 university news account).

The facility's core purpose is to provide the physical space, power, and cooling infrastructure behind Indiana University's shared computing backbone. It anchors the statewide I-Light optical fiber network that links every IU campus, houses the university's central enterprise administrative systems and servers, and hosts IU's research supercomputing clusters, including the "Big Red II+" system used for scientific and scholarly high-performance computing. A portion of the building, known internally as the "Enterprise Pod," is available for individual university departments and research groups to lease rack space for their own equipment rather than maintaining separate server rooms elsewhere on campus.

In April 2019, IU's Board of Trustees approved a roughly $12 million infrastructure-upgrade project for the Bloomington data center, covering new power-distribution units and electrical panels, uninterruptible power supply systems, emergency backup power, computer-room air-handling units and their control systems, a generator, a chiller, and water-to-water heat exchangers built specifically to support a new liquid, direct-to-server-chip cooling loop. University leadership described the goal as improving the facility's reliability and backup capability during power failures and routine maintenance, while also expanding its electrical and cooling headroom for future growth -- work consistent with a computing center approaching the end of its original infrastructure's useful life after roughly a decade of continuous, growing use.

As a university-operated facility rather than a commercial provider, IU does not publish square footage, total power capacity, or tenant and utilization figures for the Bloomington data center, and none of the public reporting on the 2019 upgrade included those numbers either. What is documented is the building's role as the operational center of the university's statewide computing network, its age, the scale of investment IU has been willing to make to keep it current, and its dual role serving both routine administrative computing and frontier research workloads from the same campus building.

reading.body:
The IU Data Center in Bloomington is the university's primary computing facility, operated since the early 2010s to host Indiana University's statewide administrative systems, enterprise services, and research supercomputing clusters including the Big Red II+ system. The facility serves as the backbone of I-Light, the optical network linking all IU campuses across the state. Its published capacity figures are not available, so the scale of its compute footprint cannot be calculated from operator specifications.

Indiana University invested roughly $12 million in infrastructure upgrades approved in 2019, targeting power distribution, backup generation, cooling systems, and liquid-cooled direct-to-chip heat exchange capability. These upgrades indicate the facility was nearing the end of its original infrastructure lifecycle after a decade of continuous growth and was being retrofitted for higher density and improved resilience. The scope and timing of this investment suggest the university anticipated sustained or increased computational demand, but the specific electrical or cooling capacity added remains unpublished.

No published megawatt figures exist for this campus. Indiana has six mapped data center facilities, of which only two report power capacity to this site, totaling 22.5 MW across the state. This campus ranks third in the state by published capacity, though that ranking reflects the absence of published figures from other facilities rather than a confirmed capacity number for Bloomington itself. As a university-operated facility rather than a commercial provider, its utilization, tenant composition, and available capacity for external workloads are not disclosed.
